read_file.description: Return the entire content of one public workspace file as a single UTF-8 string, without line numbers or truncation. Files that are not valid UTF-8 are rejected. Paths under .checks are host-private. Use read_range for large files, or when you need line numbers and the content_hash that edit_range checks.

list_files.description: List every file in the public workspace tree, recursively, as workspace-relative paths. prefix filters by plain string prefix on those paths: "src/" keeps only the src directory, while "src" also keeps paths such as "src2/a.py". Paths under .checks are never listed.

prefix.description: Optional string prefix on workspace-relative paths; end it with / to limit the list to one directory

search.description: Search public workspace files with a Python re regex. Returns path, 1-based line and snippet per match with the snapshot digest. Large results are truncated with next_cursor.

pattern.description: Python re regex searched per line

path.description: Optional file or directory scope within the public tree

cursor.description: Continuation cursor from a truncated search

read_range.description: Read a line range of one public workspace file. Returns path, start_line, end_line, total_lines, the snapshot digest and the file content_hash. Truncated output carries next_cursor.

end_line.description: Last line to read, inclusive; omit for end of file

cursor.description: Continuation cursor from a truncated read

write_file.description: Create one public workspace file or replace its entire content with UTF-8 text; missing parent directories are created. Engineering only. Paths under .checks are host-private. Use edit_range to change part of an existing file.

edit_range.description: Replace an exact original text inside one public workspace file. Engineering only. The text is located by content: when expected_text occurs exactly once in the file it is replaced wherever it is, so the line numbers may be stale; when it occurs more than once, start_line picks the occurrence starting on that line. expected_digest (the read_range file content_hash) must still match when given; otherwise the edit is rejected and the file is left unchanged.

start_line.description: First line of the span to replace, 1-based; optional, used to choose between several occurrences of expected_text

end_line.description: Last line of the span to replace, inclusive; optional, used to choose between occurrences on the same line

expected_text.description: Exact original text previously read, joined by newline without a trailing newline

new_text.description: Replacement text for the located text, lines joined by newline

expected_digest.description: File content_hash observed when the span was read; omit to skip the digest check

delete_file.description: Delete one existing regular workspace file. Engineering only; requires a reason. Directories and links are rejected.

move_file.description: Move one existing regular workspace file without overwriting. Engineering only; requires a reason. Directories and links are rejected.

run_check.description: Host-executes a check in a fresh copy of the checked snapshot and records exit_code, summary, and snapshot hash. The command string runs with bash at the copy root, in a new process with the Yudao process's full environment; the copy is deleted when the check finishes. Do not self-report exit_code. command example: "uv run pytest tests". timeout_sec is optional: when omitted it is the default; a larger value is applied at the maximum (both are rule-registered defaults). Only run_check receipts count as check evidence; bash results are action receipts.

command.description: The command string to run with bash at the copy root, e.g. uv run pytest tests

timeout_sec.description: Optional time limit in seconds; omitted uses the default, larger values apply the maximum

bash.description: Run one arbitrary shell command string with bash in this session's workspace and get the host-observed exit status, output, and whether the process was stopped. Each call is a new process with no shell state; the workspace root is the working directory. The process inherits the Yudao process's full environment, and output replaces the value of any known secret with its name. On timeout or cancellation the whole process tree is stopped and the receipt says so, with the output received until then. Output exceeding the limit is truncated with a job_id; use read_output to retrieve the remaining output. Background commands (background=true) return immediately with a job_id. A bash result is an action receipt, not a check receipt: it cannot be listed in submit_delivery check_names; run the checks a delivery needs with run_check.

command.description: Command string, e.g. uv run pytest tests

timeout_sec.description: Optional seconds; default and maximum are rule-registered

background.description: Optional boolean; when true, start the command in the background and return immediately with a job_id

read_output.description: Read new output produced since the last read for a background command or a truncated command. Returns the output chunk, status (running, exited, stopped, ended), and exit_code.

stop_job.description: Stop a running background command and its entire process tree. Returns receipt stating the process tree was stopped.

submit_product_spec.description: Submit a ProductSpec. Required: goal, requirements, acceptance_criteria, basis_product_spec_hash. basis_product_spec_hash must equal the current effective ProductSpec content_hash (or null on the first spec); a stale basis is rejected so the revision cannot proceed against a superseded PRD.

requirements.description: Must contain at least one item

acceptance_criteria.description: Must contain at least one item

changed.description: Requirements added or changed in this revision

change_record.description: Required when replacing a ProductSpec. Submit the complete new requirements and explain changed, retained, and retired behavior. A complete ProductSpec processes user input; a response or product decision does not. Omit on the first spec.

decision_changes.description: When replacing a spec, explicitly retain, integrate, or retire every effective product decision. Empty for the first spec.

basis_product_spec_hash.description: Content hash of the ProductSpec this revision is based on. Pass the current effective ProductSpec content_hash; pass null only for the first spec. The host rejects the submission if this value does not equal the current effective ProductSpec content_hash.

submit_product_decision.description: Publish an explicit product requirement decision with its rationale. This changes the effective contract.

ask.description: Ask another department a question. The step loop pauses until the recipient department answers via a branch session; the answer is returned as this tool's result. When engineering asks quality, write the question and the background in two parts instead of question and background: facts (interfaces, usage, file locations, how to run, references to host evidence) and explanation (why it is implemented this way, the judgement about correctness, the view on failures and review comments). Quality reads the facts part only until it has submitted its own conclusion on the current delivery.

facts.description: Engineering asking quality: the question and the background as facts (interfaces, usage, file locations, how to run, references to host evidence).

explanation.description: Engineering asking quality: the explanation part (why it is implemented this way, the judgement about correctness, the view on failures and review comments). Quality reads it only after it has submitted its own conclusion on the current delivery.

answer.description: Submit an answer to the current ask question, ending this branch session. Product may optionally include PRD revision parameters to update requirements. When engineering answers quality, write the answer in two parts instead of answer: facts (interfaces, usage, file locations, how to run, references to host evidence) and explanation (why it is implemented this way, the judgement about correctness, the view on failures and review comments). Quality reads the facts part only until it has submitted its own conclusion on the current delivery.

facts.description: Engineering answering quality: the answer as facts (interfaces, usage, file locations, how to run, references to host evidence).

explanation.description: Engineering answering quality: the explanation part (why it is implemented this way, the judgement about correctness, the view on failures and review comments). Quality reads it only after it has submitted its own conclusion on the current delivery.

requirements.description: Must contain at least one item

acceptance_criteria.description: Must contain at least one item

changed.description: Requirements added or changed in this revision

change_record.description: Required when replacing a ProductSpec. Submit the complete new requirements and explain changed, retained, and retired behavior. A complete ProductSpec processes user input; a response or product decision does not. Omit on the first spec.

decision_changes.description: When replacing a spec, explicitly retain, integrate, or retire every effective product decision. Empty for the first spec.

basis_product_spec_hash.description: Content hash of the ProductSpec this revision is based on. Pass the current effective ProductSpec content_hash; pass null only for the first spec. The host rejects the submission if this value does not equal the current effective ProductSpec content_hash.

submit_guidance_response.description: Respond to one persisted department guidance item. Use explained when the handling is an explanation, no change is required, or this department cannot apply it. Use completed only when host-verified actions after this guidance was adopted are listed in guidance_results; the host binds those results and result_event_ids cannot enlarge that set. Empty, rejected, failed, or earlier-unrelated results cannot complete an action. This response does not change the contract, files, or QA result by itself.

result_event_ids.description: Optional. completed must be a subset of guidance_results; the host binds those results. explained, declined, and needs_work do not require results.

submit_delivery.description: Submit a DeliverySpec after writing files and running checks. Every name in check_names must be a name you passed to run_check in this activation on the current workspace; receipts from earlier activations are not reused, and if any file changes after a check, call run_check again before submitting. bash results are action receipts and are not accepted as delivery check receipts. A name without a matching run_check receipt rejects the delivery. basis_product_spec_hash must equal the current effective ProductSpec content_hash; a stale basis is rejected so the delivery cannot proceed against a superseded PRD.

check_names.description: Names passed to run_check in this activation on the current workspace; bash results do not count

basis_product_spec_hash.description: Content hash of the ProductSpec this delivery is based on. The host rejects the submission if this value does not equal the current effective ProductSpec content_hash.

submit_review.description: Submit a QAReview. release requires quality-run host receipts with exit_code 0 on the current snapshot. Engineering receipts are not accepted as QA evidence. checks are check names. basis_delivery_spec_hash must equal the current effective DeliverySpec content_hash; a stale basis is rejected so the review cannot proceed against a superseded delivery.

checks.description: Quality check names run via run_check

basis_delivery_spec_hash.description: Content hash of the DeliverySpec this review is based on. The host rejects the submission if this value does not equal the current effective DeliverySpec content_hash.

submit_structure.description: Submit the existing-structure description of an onboarding run. Write only what requires reading several files to establish and what later work can easily get wrong: no generic advice, no complete file tree, nothing you cannot verify. Every entry in build_and_test must have a run_check receipt from this activation on the current workspace snapshot; the recorded exit status is taken from that receipt, and an exit status other than 0 is accepted as it is. Onboarding gives you no write, edit, delete or move tools, so the workspace tree must still equal the snapshot when you submit.

overall.description: How the repository is composed and how it runs

responsibility.description: What this module is responsible for

name.description: The name you passed to run_check

command.description: The command string you passed to run_check

purpose.description: What this command builds or tests

build_and_test.description: Each entry needs a run_check receipt from this activation bound to the current snapshot

requirement.description: The initial PRD requirement, written as it appears

conventions.description: Code generation, special environment variables, slow tests or tests that need an external service

submit_baseline_review.description: Submit the baseline review of an onboarding run. Do not apply the release rules of a normal work item: a check that exits non-zero does not by itself reject the baseline. conclusions carries exactly one conclusion for every requirement of the current initial PRD, with status verified (evidence names a passing check), read_only (evidence gives the location that supports it), existing_defect (evidence names the failing check) or unsupported (code, documentation and tests none of them support the description). checks are the run_check receipts of this activation bound to the current snapshot and the current ProductSpec, at least one, and the recorded exit status is taken from the receipt. Every check with a non-zero exit status that no existing_defect conclusion references must appear in other_failures with the reason. consistent requires no unsupported conclusion, no omission and no unexplained failing check; rework_product requires at least one unsupported conclusion or one omission. Engineering receipts are not accepted as QA evidence.

requirement.description: The initial PRD requirement, written as it appears

evidence.description: A passing check name, a location, or the failing check name

capability.description: An outward-facing capability missing from the initial PRD

location.description: Where it lives in the repository, workspace-relative

checks.description: Baseline check names run via run_check in this activation

reason.description: Why it fails, for example it needs network or an external service
